# Round 2 memo: what is scaling together across regions, and where we still disagree

**Basis:** web searches run on 12 Oct 2026, plus the two files you prepared, `research/output/market_prices.json` and `research/output/valuations.json` (Yahoo closes 11 Oct 2021 → 9 Oct 2026; GCC to 8 Oct). Where I quote returns from your files, "adj." means the adjusted-close return and the rest are price-only. Facts from web searches came mostly from search-layer summaries of releases, so the important ones still need checking against the primary documents. No edits or external actions.

---

## 1. Your two objections

### 1a. "Broad grid modernization is not occurring": I withdraw it. I keep a narrower version.

You're right. Itron alone can't identify that claim, and evidence from other regions contradicts it:

- **China:** State Grid's fixed-asset investment was over RMB 310B in H1 2026, up 12.6%. Fifteen ultra-high-voltage (UHV) projects and **37 pumped-storage stations** are under accelerated construction. The 15th Five-Year Plan budgets RMB 4T, 40% more than the previous plan ([SMM](https://news.metal.com/newscontent/104022862-state-grids-h1-fixed-asset-investment-exceeds-rmb-310-bn-up-126-yoy-new-energy-capacity-hits-155-bn-kw), [ARC](https://www.arcweb.com/blog/state-grids-plan-invest-rmb-4-trillion-during-chinas-15th-five-year-plan-period)).
- **India:** Power Grid's Q1 FY27 capex was ₹7,765 crore, up 11.2%. FY26 capex of about ₹39,967 crore beat its guidance ([T&D India](https://www.tndindia.com/pgcil-records-11-per-cent-capex-growth-in-q1fy27-capitalization-trebles/amp/)).
- **Europe:** Prysmian's Q2 Transmission revenue grew 14.3% organically at a 21.2% margin, and it raised guidance ([Prysmian](https://www.prysmian.com/en/media/press-releases/prysmian-raises-guidance-after-its-best-quarter-yet)). Siemens Energy's Grid Technologies backlog is €51B (Round 1). Your NKT and Hitachi Energy India figures add to this.
- **Itron argues against me as well.** Its Networked Solutions hardware fell 17%, but Outcomes (software and services) rose 13% and annual recurring revenue rose 21% to $417M ([8-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000780571/000117184326004912/exh_991.htm)). That is control-layer growth inside the company I used as the counterexample.

**What I keep:** the growth is uneven across segments. Transmission, HV cable, transformers and interconnectors are booming in every region. Distribution metering hardware runs on its own cycle. Labor-heavy T&D contractors show mixed results: MYR's T&D revenue grew only about 3.5%, and India's KEC had flat revenue, a 41% profit drop and a share price −69% from its 2024 close. I accept your synthesis: **system-wide grid buildout that varies by segment, plus concentrated data-center power.**

**A disagreement I want to keep open:** most of this grid spending would happen **without AI**. Europe's drivers are offshore wind, interconnectors and security. India's driver is a 260 GW heat-driven peak. China's driver is integrating roughly 200 GW/yr of renewables. On this evidence, "AI and electrification are paired" is partly coincidental: several separate drivers are converging on the same scarce equipment. That matters for whether the pairing survives an AI slowdown. My answer is that grid demand mostly survives it and data-center-specific demand does not.

### 1b. Nvidia revenue vs. hyperscaler capex: I accept the critique and retract the global claim

Annualizing one quarter, overlapping customer sets and double counting make that ratio unusable as a share of spending. I retract "most spending is on short-lived assets" as a global statement. I replace it with your company-specific evidence: Microsoft discloses that about two-thirds of its Q4 capex went to short-lived assets. The structural point survives only in narrower form: **where it is disclosed, stranding risk sits mostly in short-lived compute.**

Indirect support from your dataset: Micron is up 1,387%, and in China the hardware chokepoints soared (Cambricon +1,692%, SMIC +163%, Foxconn Industrial Internet adj. +432%). Those are signs of where scarcity sat. They are not a measure of how capex divides between asset types.

---

## 2. AAON and Hammond backlog: completion or turning demand?

**My verdict: mainly conversion and lumpiness, with one weak early demand signal at Hammond. Demand has not turned yet.**

| Evidence | Points to conversion | Points to demand turning |
|---|---|---|
| Hammond: backlog −6.9% QoQ "as shipments exceeded new order bookings"; expanded plants are converting more orders into shipments; record shipments ([GlobeNewswire](https://www.globenewswire.com/news-release/2026/07/30/3336509/0/en/Hammond-Power-Solutions-Reports-Q2-2026-Financial-Results.html), [MarketBeat](https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/hammond-power-solutions-q2-earnings-call-highlights-2026-08-01/)) | ✔ | |
| Hammond: Canada −23.7%, "general softness and **increasingly competitive pricing**" | | ✔ (weak, regional) |
| AAON: backlog −7.4% QoQ, which management attributes to faster conversion and the timing of large BASX awards. The release says "booking activity remained solid" ([AAON](https://investors.aaon.com/investor-news/aaon-reports-record-second-quarter-2026-results-driven-by-strong-demand-accelerating-throughput-and-improved-operating-execution)) | ✔ | |
| AAON: gross margin 26.6% → 24.3% from the Memphis ramp and outsourced components. TTM free cash flow is **−$119M** with capex of $205M (your valuations file) | Ramp cost, a supply-side problem | |
| Same quarter: Powell's book-to-bill was 3.0× and Fluence had record orders. Large orders arrive in lumps | ✔ | |

**Inference:** two capacity-constrained suppliers expanded capacity and burned down backlog. That is the supply response we predicted in Round 1, and it is the **precursor** to price competition, not proof of it. Demand turning would look like this:

- **Falsification test:** in their next reports (AAON ~5 Nov; Hammond ~late Oct/Nov), bookings stay below shipments for **two more quarters**, **and** pricing language spreads beyond Canada or gross margins fall after the ramp costs are gone.

If only the first condition holds, it is a normalizing order flow, not a demand peak.

---

## 3. What is scaling together that isn't obvious

Each item below is a sourced physical or financial fact plus my inference about the link.

### 3.1 Chinese manufacturing deflation becomes Gulf, European and Indian deployment, and Chinese shareholders don't capture it

- **Facts:**
  - China's new-type storage additions **fell 18%** in H1 2026, while its overseas storage orders **jumped 83%** ([ESS News](https://www.ess-news.com/2026/08/28/china-h1-2026-new-type-energy-storage-additions-fall-18-overseas-orders-jump-83/)).
  - In July 2026, BYD-supplied **2.5 GW / 12.5 GWh** was commissioned in Saudi Arabia, putting Saudi monthly utility-scale installations ahead of China's. Gotion is supplying 6 GWh of Saudi Arabia's first BESS tender, and a Chinese-Saudi JV is building an 18 GWh factory with the first phase due Q1 2027 ([energy-storage.news](https://www.energy-storage.news/gotion-to-supply-6gwh-of-battery-storage-for-saudi-arabias-first-utility-scale-bess-tender/), [Yahoo/MEED](https://finance.yahoo.com/sectors/energy/articles/chinese-saudi-joint-venture-build-121828135.html)).
  - CATL storage revenue was RMB 53.26B (+87.5%) at a 23.96% gross margin, down 1.56pt ([ESS News](https://www.ess-news.com/2026/07/27/catl-storage-revenue-jumps-88-as-h1-profit-hits-cny-43-3-billion/)).
  - Sungrow's H1 revenue fell 29%, with declines concentrated in **domestic and Middle East** markets. Storage still became 50% of revenue, but its margin fell 7.5pt ([energy-storage.news](https://www.energy-storage.news/sungrows-battery-storage-revenue-tops-pv-business-h1-shipments-hit-25gwh/)).
- **Your file:** CATL is −19% YTD (2025 close 367 → 298). Sungrow is **−53% YTD** (171 → 80.7). LONGi is −80% over five years.
- **Inference:** the most important cross-region flow of 2026 is Chinese electrochemical capacity moving into GCC grids. The surplus goes to buyers, through falling margins. The Iran war is a direct risk to this flow; Sungrow names the Middle East as a source of its decline.

### 3.2 Indian engineering and labor are the build layer for the Gulf, and they absorb Gulf war risk

- **Facts:**
  - At L&T, international is 52% of the ₹7.79T order book, the Middle East is **71% of international**, and Europe is 14%. That puts the Middle East at about 37% of the total book (my arithmetic).
  - International was 56% of Q1 inflow, including large European offshore-wind wins.
  - Management cites Middle East supply-chain disruption as weighing on revenue ([DSIJ](https://insights.dsij.in/dsijarticledetail/rs-779-lakh-crore-record-order-book-infrastructure-major-reports-14-yoy-growth-in-q1-fy27-profit-check-details-58649), [PL India](https://www.plindia.com/pl-research/larsen-toubro-lt-in-q1fy27-result-update-mixed-q1-healthy-inflows-amid-execution-headwinds-buy/)).
  - KEC's Q1 profit fell 41% with an EBITDA margin of 5.8%, despite its largest-ever Saudi T&D order in March 2026 ([Business Today](https://www.businesstoday.in/markets/stocks/story/kec-international-shares-hit-52-week-low-q1-earnings-hit-investor-sentiment-549155-2026-08-14)).
- **Your file:** L&T +116% over five years but −9% YTD. KEC −69% from its 2024 close. Hitachi Energy India +1,167% and ABB India +270%, both equipment suppliers with export books.
- **Inference:** inside India, **equipment makers with pricing power beat fixed-price EPC contractors**. Contractors carry execution and geopolitical risk; equipment makers carry scarcity. It is the same split as US Powell vs. MYR, but sharper. On top of that, INR fell 28.6% against the USD, which leaves INDA roughly flat in USD (adj. +0.6%).

### 3.3 The Gulf scales gas, batteries, water and compute together, under fire

- **Facts:**
  - Saudi Arabia has roughly 30 GW of gas generation under construction, and SEC has reportedly booked about 30 GW of turbine slots ahead ([MEED](https://guest.meed.com/saudi-electricity-company-eyes-30gw-capacity)). This is a 2025 source; the 2026 tally is **not sourced**.
  - Batteries are being commissioned alongside the gas (above).
  - Your ACWA data: actual H1 additions were 0.8 GWh of BESS and 0.9M m³/day of water, against a stated 98.2 GW portfolio. Delivered capacity is a small fraction of the headline.
  - Compute: Humain targets 1.9 GW by 2030, starting with up to 100 MW sites ([Sharikat Mubasher](https://en.sharikatmubasher.com/media-hub/news/21503220/humain-to-open-data-centers-in-riyadh-dammam-in-early-2026)). Iran's IRGC explicitly threatened Stargate UAE in April 2026 ([TechRadar](https://www.techradar.com/ai-platforms-assistants/iran-is-threatening-to-bomb-the-usd30-billion-stargate-ai-data-center-backed-by-openai-nvidia-and-other-tech-giants)).
  - Whether Stargate UAE's first 200 MW is commissioned: **not sourced**.
- **Your file:** ACWA −59% from its 2024 close. KSA adj. −3%, QAT adj. −4%, UAE adj. +61%, Emaar adj. +279%, Aramco adj. +7%.
- **Inference:** GCC capital is building physical capability at scale, but **listed returns accrue to the hub (UAE real estate and finance), not the builders**. Data centers there are now military targets, so resilience is a priced constraint, not an abstraction.

### 3.4 Real-estate capital moves from human space to machine space in both the US and China

- **Facts:** US office values are −34% from the 2022 peak (Green Street, Round 1) while North American data-center vacancy is 1.4%. Your source: China property investment −19.9% and new starts −24.8% Jan–Aug 2026, while State Grid capex is +12.6%. In June, China's electricity use for internet data services grew **+41.4%** and for EV charging/battery swapping **+57.1%** ([SMM/NEA](https://news.metal.com/en/newscontent/104023410-national-energy-administration-total-electricity-consumption-up-53-yoy-january-june)).
- **Your file:** BXP adj. −33% vs. EQIX adj. +51% and DLR adj. +52%.
- **Inference:** the composition of physical capital formation is shifting, in both systems, from structures for people to structures for machines and wires. I think this is the most non-obvious co-movement in the dataset.

### 3.5 Incumbency beats new build

- **Your file:**
  - Existing, interconnected, dispatchable capacity: VST adj. +901%, CEG adj. +637% (from Jan 2022), XLE adj. +175%, XOM adj. +227%, LNG adj. +188%, CAT adj. +352%.
  - New-build renewables: ORSTED −84%, VWS −15%, TAN −46%, FLNC −79%, ENPH −80%, PLUG −94%.
  - FSLR is +74%, so the pattern isn't uniform. It is a policy-protected, non-Chinese supplier.
- **Inference:** while the interconnection queue takes 5+ years and turbines are sold out, the scarce asset is **an existing grid position**. That is coordination capital (permits, interconnection rights, sites) priced as equity. CAT's link to gensets and engines for data centers is my inference; its segment data is **not sourced**.

### 3.6 Europe: the wires won and the generators lost

- **Facts:** about 700 GW of renewable and large-load projects sit in European connection queues. Denmark's grid operator Energinet **paused new connections** in March 2026 after queued consumption passed 60 GW, more than 8× its 2024 peak ([Environment+Energy Leader citing Ember](https://environmentenergyleader.com/stories/europe-has-power-to-spare-but-not-the-wires-to-move-it,133074)). Europe's data centers use about 2–3% of electricity ([Rabobank](https://www.rabobank.com/knowledge/d011517320-data-center-growth-in-europe-expands-to-emerging-markets)).
- **Your file:** NKT +258%, Prysmian adj. +349%, Schneider adj. +110%, against Ørsted and Vestas.
- **Inference:** Europe's constraint is transmission and permitting, not generation or AI load.

### 3.7 Shared global constraints: capital cost, metals and trust

- **Your file:** TLT adj. −34%, IEF adj. −9%; the 10-year yield above 5% in September (Round 1). Copper +52%, silver +168%, gold +140%. LONGi explicitly blames silver costs for its losses.
- **Inference:** gold up 140%, alongside war, reserve diversification and record fiscal deficits, suggests the **trust and coordination layer is being repriced**, not only energy. Gold doesn't buy any capability, but it measures demand for assets outside the system.
- Cybersecurity prices (CRWD +350%, PANW +403%) show the market sees trust as infrastructure. Prices are not evidence of investment volume, though; I have **no sourced spending figures**.

---

## 4. Evidence of control and coordination investment that actually happened (not just proposed)

| Mechanism | Status | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Google: **1 GW of data-center load contractually curtailable**, across 5 US utilities, with bill credits and clawback penalties | Contracted, filed with regulators | [Google blog](https://blog.google/innovation-and-ai/infrastructure-and-cloud/global-network/demand-response-data-center-milestone/), [Enlit](https://www.enlit.world/library/google-inks-demand-response-deal-with-midwest-us-utility-to-support-grid-reliability) |
| ERCOT "Batch Zero" large-load framework (≥75 MW) approved 18 Jun 2026. Texas SB6 imposes curtailment obligations on large loads. The governor's audit came on 3 Aug | Enacted rules | [Troutman](https://www.troutman.com/insights/texas-hits-pause-on-data-center-grid-connections-amid-growing-oversight-push.html) |
| Energinet connection pause; PJM capacity-price cap | Administrative rationing, which is coordination by restriction | above; Round 1 |
| Itron Outcomes +13%, ARR $417M (+21%) | Delivered revenue | [8-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000780571/000117184326004912/exh_991.htm) |
| State Grid: 37 pumped-storage stations, 15 UHV lines; US storage about 52 GW (your EIA source); Saudi 12.5 GWh commissioned | Physical flexibility under construction or delivered | above |
| India met its 256–260 GW peak "without shortage," with solar at 21.5% of peak supply | Operational outcome | [Renewable Watch](https://renewablewatch.in/2026/04/29/india-meets-its-all-time-peak-electricity-demand-of-256-gw-mop/), [Energetica](https://www.energetica-india.net/news/india-meets-record-256-gw-peak-power-demand-without-shortage-solar-contributes-21-5-percent) |
| Grid software orders (GE Vernova GridOS, Siemens) | **Not sourced.** I found product pages only | n/a |

**Observation:** most of the 2026 coordination "investment" is **institutional**: rules, queues, caps, curtailment contracts. Relatively little is capitalized software. Institutions are scaling by rationing access. That supports the idea of coordination as the binding layer, and contradicts any claim that it scales smoothly.

---

## 5. Candidate joint conclusion

> **What societies are scaling (2021–2026) is reliable, deployable capability: useful work and information processing delivered where and when needed, under enforceable rules.** Energy and compute are necessary inputs, not the objective.
>
> Capability is limited by whichever complement binds: materials (copper, silver, transformers), energy (firm power), information (chips, memory), trust and coordination (interconnection rights, permits, contracts, security), labor (EPC, electricians), or ecology (water, heat, emissions).
>
> **The binding constraint migrates:**
> - 2021–22: European gas and energy prices
> - 2023–24: accelerators and memory
> - 2025–26: interconnection, turbines, transformers, permits
> - 2026: war and the cost of capital, layered on top
>
> **Financial returns accrue to whoever holds the currently binding constraint and decay when supply responds.** Owners of commoditized deployed hardware (Chinese PV and storage, offshore wind developers) pass the surplus to users even while the physical build succeeds.

**On resilience:** I'd treat it as a **constraint with measurable variables** (reserve margins, PJM's 6.6 GW shortfall, Hormuz transits, the share of capacity within strike range), not as a co-equal objective. Redundancy lowers measured efficiency, and calling it an objective makes the framework unfalsifiable. That is a disagreement for you to push on.

**Why this is falsifiable:** it predicts in advance that margins compress where lead times shorten and backlog-to-delivery ratios fall, and that they persist where they don't. Tests:

- Turbine slots (GE Vernova reaches 20 → 24 GW/yr)
- Transformer lead times below ~80 weeks by 2028
- AAON/Hammond pricing over the next 2 quarters
- Whether VST/CEG-type incumbency premia shrink as the interconnection backlog clears

## 6. Proposed consensus

1. Physical buildout and shareholder returns are separate. Our 120-asset dataset shows many cases of each without the other (Ørsted/LONGi/Sungrow/ACWA vs. Powell/Hammond/Hitachi Energy India).
2. Grid investment is global and varies by segment. Transmission, HV cable and transformers lead in every region we checked. Distribution hardware and fixed-price EPC lag.
3. Data-center power is a concentrated layer on top of grid spending, not its main driver outside the US.
4. China is the world's electrotech manufacturing base. In 2026 its marginal storage output goes overseas, especially to the GCC.
5. India supplies equipment and engineering labor to the Gulf and Europe, and carries Gulf geopolitical risk.
6. Coordination is advancing mainly through rationing institutions (queues, caps, curtailment contracts, audits).
7. Currency and rates materially change regional conclusions (INR −28.6%, 10-year above 5%).
8. Announcements and pipelines (Bloom's 25 GW, ACWA's 98 GW, Reliance's 3 GW, Humain's 6 GW) are not deliveries, and must be reported next to actual commissioning.

## 7. Unresolved, with my position

| Question | My position | Evidence that would settle it |
|---|---|---|
| Is the AI–electrification pairing causal or coincidental? | Mostly coincidental outside the US | Grid capex growth in an AI-capex down year |
| Is ordering near peak (US data-center equipment)? | Not yet; conversion phase | Bookings < shipments for 2 quarters across AAON, Hammond, Vertiv, Modine |
| Do current multiples already price this in (POWL fwd 29.7×, VRT 30.8×, PWR 38.3× vs ITRI 13.2×)? | Largely yes for bottleneck holders | Margin path after supply additions |
| Is gold's +140% a coordination/trust signal or a monetary one? | Both; can't separate them yet | Central-bank purchase data vs. real yields (not sourced) |
| Resilience: objective or constraint? | Constraint | Agree on metrics first |
| Gulf data centers under strike risk: delay or relocation? | Unknown | Stargate UAE and Humain commissioning dates |

**Gaps:** China's Jan–Aug electricity total (only an unconfirmed +4.3% from a Turkish-language report), SEC 2026 capex, Prysmian/NKT backlog (I'm relying on your NKT figure), grid-software order data, CAT's data-center revenue, and Stargate UAE status.

**For you to challenge:** (1) my "coincidental pairing" claim, (2) my treatment of resilience as a constraint, and (3) whether "returns go to whoever owns the binding constraint" can be specified tightly enough to test.
